text: I'll start with the paged Deployment and its pod.

remediation.name: checkout-worker
remediation.required_value: env entry named AMQP_URL carrying the queue connection URL, e.g. - name: AMQP_URL, value: amqp://<user>:<pass>@<broker-host>:5672/ (or a valueFrom secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef pointing at an object that actually holds that key)

arguments.root_cause_statement: The Deployment payments/checkout-worker declares a container "worker" whose command begins with a guard: `[ -n "${AMQP_URL:-}" ] || { echo "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"; exit 1; }`. The pod template supplies no environment at all — there is no env, no envFrom, and no ConfigMap or Secret in the namespace that could carry the value (the only ConfigMap in payments is kube-root-ca.crt and there are no Secrets). Every container start therefore hits the guard, prints "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set" and exits 1, so kubelet restarts it into CrashLoopBackOff (5 restarts recorded), the single replica never becomes Ready, and the Deployment stays 0/1 Ready, which is what the availability monitor paged on and why checkout jobs are never consumed from the queue.
arguments.mechanism: The Deployment payments/checkout-worker has no AMQP_URL entry in .spec.template.spec.containers[worker].env (the rendered container shows "Environment: <none>"), while that container's command requires it: `[ -n "${AMQP_URL:-}" ] || { echo "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"; exit 1; }`. Each start of the worker container therefore exits with code 1 after logging "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set", kubelet backs it off into CrashLoopBackOff, and the Deployment's only replica never reaches Ready so it reports 0/1.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment reports 0/1 Ready and its only pod is crash-looping.
The worker container is in CrashLoopBackOff after repeated Error exits.
The Deployment pod template's worker container requires AMQP_URL and exits 1 when it is unset, yet the template defines no env or envFrom.
evidence.quote: "[ -n \"${AMQP_URL:-}\" ] || { echo \"FATAL: AMQP_URL not set\"; exit 1; }; echo \"connected to queue at ${AMQP_URL}\"; while :; do echo \"consuming checkout jobs\"; sleep 10; done"

evidence.claim: The running container has no environment variables at all, and terminated with exit code 1.
The previous container instance died on exactly the missing-variable guard.
The container's last termination was Error/exit code 1, matching the guard's exit 1.
No ConfigMap in the namespace could have supplied AMQP_URL; the only one present is the kube API CA bundle.
No Secret exists in the namespace that could have supplied AMQP_URL either.
evidence.quote: 0 objects of kind secrets in namespace payments

ruled_out.alternative: Image pull failure or bad image reference causing the crash loop
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The image is present on the node and the container is created and started successfully on each attempt; it dies afterwards in its own command.
ruled_out.quote: Container image "busybox:1.36" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod

ruled_out.alternative: Scheduling or node capacity problem keeping the pod from running
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod was scheduled and is Running with PodScheduled True; the failure occurs after container start.

ruled_out.alternative: A broken ConfigMap or Secret key reference (envFrom/valueFrom pointing at a missing key), which would show as CreateContainerConfigError
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod template contains no env or envFrom stanza at all, so nothing is being resolved incorrectly — the variable is simply never declared.

ruled_out.alternative: ServiceAccount/RBAC identity problem preventing the worker from operating
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod runs under the default ServiceAccount and its token volume mounts fine; the container fails on its own environment guard before any API call.
